note: Photo copy specs for ops/photos-copy. One target listing per spec. frames = the source listing's live images in display order. image = the Etsy image id on the source listing; the copy runs only while the live gallery is exactly this list. file = the frame's original file on the panel's own domain (public/ in this repo) and sha256 = that file's hash; these are the bytes that get uploaded. alt = the alt text written on the target, which is also how a copied frame is recognised there. If the target holds an image that is neither the placeholder nor one of these frames, nothing is written.

elongated-cable-7in.note: Private custom order listing; its only image was Etsy's placeholder graphic. The ten frames are the parent listing's live gallery, viewed on 2026-11-17: no text, no length and no karat on any frame. Frame 9 shows the design in yellow, white and rose gold; the other nine show yellow gold. Bytes come from the original files in public/artifact/him26/B10, not from Etsy's image servers: on 2026-11-17 the same Etsy image address returned different files to different clients for six of the ten frames. Each original was measured against the live frame it stands for: mean pixel difference 0.36 to 0.63 of 255 at 256 px (two different frames differ by 57 to 90), so they are the same ten pictures in the same order. Alt texts name no karat and no length; only frame 9 names metal colors, because that is what the frame shows.
